explanations: luna: 1:6 asks God to guide the speaker to the straight path. This gives a direct route to the source-section’s arrow-point image of guidance, although the verse does not describe a crafted object.
terra: God creates everything on earth, turns to heaven, and proportions it as seven heavens; creation proceeds into the ordered finishing of a constructed whole.
terra: Twelve springs emerge and every people knows its drinking place; water is divided into recognized shares for a whole community.
terra: Those who buy worldly life with the Hereafter enact the section’s choice as an exchange, and their punishment is neither lightened nor relieved.
terra: Those who purchase magic know that its buyer has no khalaq in the Hereafter; the bargain turns a chosen worldly acquisition into loss of the enduring share.
terra: God desires ease rather than hardship, commands completion of the numbered period, and calls for magnifying Him because He guided; ease, measure, guidance, and glorification converge.

luna: 2:200 says the person who asks only for worldly good has no “خَلَاقٍ” in the Hereafter. The source-section identifies خَلَاق as a measured share, so this is a direct instance of a worldly choice leaving no afterlife share. | terra: The worshipper who asks the Lord only for this world has “no khalaq in the Hereafter”; the Quran uses the section’s measured-share noun for precisely Surah 87’s worldly choice.
terra: Beside 2:200’s person with no afterlife share, this speaker asks the Lord for good in both worlds, showing a choice of portion that does not discard the lasting life.

luna: 2:202 says those people have “نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟,” a share from what they earned. It clarifies the source-section’s contrast between a lot-won share and a share assigned in relation to what one has done. | terra: Those who ask for both worlds “have a share” (نَصِيبٌ) of what they earned, completing 2:200–201’s contrast between a passing request and a valid final allotment.

luna: 2:219 asks about intoxicants and gambling and says their sin is greater than their benefit, “نَفْعِهِمَا.” It joins the source-section’s meysir game to its named root ن ف ع and distinguishes a game’s benefit from its greater harm. | terra: Wine and gambling have benefits but their sin is greater than their benefit; the judgment directly tests the section’s water-skin term nifʿ against the apparent gain of maysir.
terra: A divorce gift is due according to the affluent person’s measure and the constrained person’s measure; a human obligation is fitted to capacity rather than won by lot.

luna: 2:280 says an insolvent debtor should be given time until ease, using the source-section root ي س ر in a financial setting. It contrasts ease granted to someone in need with meysir as a game for dividing gains.

luna: 3:6 says God forms people in their mothers’ wombs as He wills. This is a bodily instance of the source-section’s making and fitting a form to its intended measure. | terra: God forms people in the womb however He wills; hidden bodily formation supplies the concrete workshop implied by measuring before shaping.

luna: 3:44 recalls people casting their pens to decide who would care for Mary. It stages a lot that assigns a responsibility rather than a game’s prize, clarifying the boundary around the source-section’s arrow-drawn shares. | terra: The contenders cast their pens to determine who would care for Mary; this narrative allocation by cast objects provides a boundary alongside the forbidden fortune arrows.
terra: People who sell God’s covenant and their oaths for a small price have no khalaq in the Hereafter; the ayah opposes a cheap chosen return to God’s lasting portion.
terra: Every soul’s death has a written appointed term, and the ayah then gives worldly reward to its seeker and afterlife reward to its seeker; limit, selection, and allotted return occur together.

luna: 4:7 gives men and women a prescribed share in inheritance. It contrasts a legally assigned portion with the arbitrary meysir shares in the source-section. | terra: Men and women each receive an obligatory allotted share from what parents and relatives leave, whether little or much; the share is fixed rather than won by chance.

luna: 4:10 says those who consume orphan property unjustly will burn in fire. In the same inheritance passage as assigned shares, it joins the source-section’s measured allotment to its fire verb and marks unjustly taking another’s portion as its reversal.

luna: 4:11 specifies children’s inheritance fractions as divine instruction. The fixed shares contrast with the chance allocation of the source-section’s lot game. | terra: The prescribed fractional inheritances allocate a defined share to each relative as an obligation from God, a lawful counterpart to meat divided by gambling arrows.

luna: 4:12 assigns spouses and relatives specific inheritance shares, another concrete contrast between measured allotment and game-drawn shares. | terra: This ayah specifies further fractional shares for spouses and siblings, extending 4:11’s divine apportionment with distinct, bounded portions.
luna: 4:13 calls the inheritance rules “حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ” and promises success to those who obey. It completes the share assignments of 4:11–12 as divinely set limits.
luna: 4:14 warns against crossing those limits and names the Fire. It supplies the boundary and consequence for the measured shares immediately preceding it.
terra: Men have a share of what they earn and women have a share of what they earn, while all are told to ask God for His bounty; portion and giver remain distinct.
terra: Worldly enjoyment is called little and the Hereafter better for the God-fearing, another explicit comparison of the near share with the final one.
terra: Whoever desires worldly reward is told that both worldly and afterlife reward are with God, relocating the chooser’s sought share within the giver’s larger store.

luna: 5:3 explicitly forbids “أَن تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَٰمِ,” seeking a share by divining arrows. It names the exact lot-arrow practice developed in the source-section and establishes its boundary. | terra: Seeking allotted shares by divining arrows (تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَٰمِ) is forbidden, directly staging the section’s arrow-based search for a portion.

luna: 5:90 names “ٱلْمَيْسِرُ” and “ٱلْأَزْلَٰمُ” together, then says “فَٱجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ.” It directly connects the source-section’s lot-game to the roots of 87:11 (avoid) and 87:14 (succeed), while marking the game as forbidden. | terra: Wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are declared defilement, then “avoid it so that you may prosper” joins the very lot scene to 87’s roots for avoidance and flourishing.

luna: 5:91 says gambling breeds enmity and blocks remembrance of God and prayer. It completes 5:90 by showing what the source-section’s forbidden lot-game does to relations and worship. | terra: This ayah explains 5:90’s ban: gambling creates enmity and blocks remembrance of God and prayer, setting the lot against the remembrance and prayer reached in Surah 87.

luna: 5:95 requires a judged equivalent animal as an offering for game killed during pilgrimage. It connects animal distribution and measured equivalence to the source-section’s game shares, and its offering term belongs to the root ه د ي that the section connects to an arrowhead.
luna: 5:96 distinguishes sea game as lawful provision from land game forbidden during pilgrimage. It completes 5:95’s hunting penalty with a clear boundary around what may be taken as food.

luna: 6:2 joins creation from clay to a decreed term. The source-section’s definition of ق د ر as a thing’s extent and endpoint makes this a specific instance of creation bounded by a term. | terra: God creates humans from clay and then decrees a term, with another named term kept with Him; created life is bounded by two explicitly appointed limits.
terra: Those who deny revelation are said not to appraise God with His true appraisal; the same measure root judges a false estimate of the One who measures creation.
terra: The sun and moon are made for reckoning, and this is called the precise determination of the Mighty, the Knowing; cosmic regularity displays measure as calculated order.

luna: 6:136 describes people assigning shares of crops and livestock between God and their partners. It is a concrete human division of provision that contrasts with the source-section’s measured share from the Lord. | terra: People arbitrarily assign shares of crops and cattle to God and their partners; their invented division exposes the difference between fabricated allotment and the Creator’s measure.
terra: People invent restrictions on cattle and crops, allowing only whomever they choose to consume them; their arbitrary allocation continues the false division exposed in 6:136.
terra: They assign what is in certain animals’ wombs to their males, exclude their wives, and share it only if stillborn; human whim intrudes on both hidden creation and allotment.

luna: 6:152 commands full measure and weight in justice, then says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity. It connects the source-section’s measured making and shares to a just human measure fitted to capacity.
luna: 6:160 assigns tenfold return for good and only its equivalent for evil. Its explicit ratio is a measured afterlife share, unlike a meysir prize decided by arrows.
terra: The speaker says his Lord guided him to a straight path, the upright religion of Abraham; guidance, straightness, Lord, and the surah’s named patriarch meet in one claim.
luna: 7:8 says weighing on that day is the truth and names the heavy scales. It links the source-section’s measured allotment to a just measure of deeds.
luna: 7:9 says those whose scales are light have lost themselves. Its reversed result clarifies that the source-section’s choice of share has consequences beyond a worldly draw.
luna: 7:85 commands the people of Midian not to short measure or deprive people of their due. It gives a direct ethical boundary around the source-section’s making and dividing by measured portions.
terra: The twelve tribes receive twelve springs and each people knows its drinking place, repeating the scene of apportioned access to water.
luna: 8:41 assigns fixed portions of war gains to named recipients, including orphans, the needy, and travelers. These measured shares contrast with the source-section’s chance-drawn meysir portions.

luna: 9:34 warns against hoarding gold and silver instead of spending in God’s way. It gives a concrete reversal to the source-section’s worldly share: accumulated wealth becomes a liability rather than an enduring portion.

luna: 9:35 describes the hoarded metal heated in Hell’s fire and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs. It joins the source-section’s fire and measured worldly shares to its root ج ن ب for a thing’s sides, as a punishment rather than a useful vessel.
terra: The question “are you content with worldly life rather than the Hereafter?” treats the two lives as an explicit selection, then measures worldly enjoyment as little beside the next.

luna: 9:69 says earlier communities enjoyed their “خَلَاقِهِمْ” and then their deeds came to nothing in this life and the next. The source-section’s dictionary sense of خَلَاق as a measured share makes their enjoyed portion a direct parallel with its warning about choosing worldly gain. | terra: Earlier peoples enjoyed their khalaq, and the present people enjoy theirs likewise before their works fail in both worlds; an allotted share can thus be consumed as passing enjoyment.
terra: God measures the moon into stations so people can know years and calculation; measured stages give a created light a course and an intelligible end.
terra: Those who want worldly life and its adornment are paid their deeds there in full; the apparently complete near-world allotment is bounded by 11:16’s outcome.
terra: For the people described in 11:15 there is nothing in the Hereafter but fire, so payment of a worldly share proves loss when the final destination is counted.

luna: 11:84 places Shuayb’s warning against short measure in a community described as prosperous. It makes the source-section’s measure-and-share image a warning against turning provision into deprivation.
luna: 11:85 commands full measure and weight in justice and forbids diminishing people’s goods. It completes 11:84 with the same ethical limit relevant to the source-section’s shares.
terra: God subjects the sun and moon, each running to an appointed term, and directs the affair; created motion is aimed toward a fixed endpoint.

luna: 13:8 says everything with God is by “مِقْدَارٍ” while describing what wombs carry. It gives the source-section’s measure-and-endpoint claim a specific created-life instance. | terra: God knows what every womb bears, what it diminishes and increases, and “every thing with Him is by a measure”; the womb makes hidden variation part of exact apportionment.

luna: 13:17 says rain makes valleys flow according to their capacity, while foam passes and what benefits people remains. It offers a specific image of measured capacity, fleeting excess, and retained benefit beside the source-section’s useful vessel and measured shares. | terra: Flood foam and smelting dross vanish, while what benefits people remains; useful material, fire-work, benefit, and endurance meet in a single craftsman-like parable.

terra: God expands provision or measures it narrowly, while people rejoice in worldly life even though it is only a brief enjoyment beside the Hereafter; measure and Surah 87’s mistaken preference coincide.
terra: Those who prefer worldly life over the Hereafter and divert from God’s way combine the lower choice with a crooked course.

luna: 14:17 describes death approaching the person from every side in torment, yet he does not die. This is a specific fire-boundary parallel to 87:12–13 and clarifies the source-section’s line about neither dying nor living.
terra: Abraham asks his Lord to keep him and his children away from idol worship; the surah’s named patriarch voices a positive form of the avoidance root.
terra: The earth brings forth “every thing measured” (مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ); living provision itself appears fitted to weight and proportion.

luna: 15:21 says nothing is sent down except by a known measure, in a passage about what is with God and what He sends. This concretizes the source-section’s measured making as measured provision. | terra: Every thing’s treasuries are with God, and He sends it down only in a known measure; this distinguishes the true giver’s measured allotment from a share won by chance.
terra: God describes proportioning the human form before breathing spirit into it, making تسوية a preparatory stage with a directed completion.

luna: 16:9 says God’s is the direction of the way, while some ways are crooked. The source-section’s bent stick made straight and arrow guided toward a target give this contrast a concrete shape. | terra: God is responsible for the path’s right direction while some paths deviate; this is the moral boundary between the straightened, pointed course and crooked alternatives.
terra: Every people receives the command to worship God and avoid false gods; the same ayah then distinguishes those God guided from those upon whom error took hold, joining avoidance to direction.
luna: 16:68 says the Lord inspires the bee to make homes. It gives the source-section’s claim that the Maker also directs a creature a concrete case of guidance fitted to a creature’s work.

luna: 16:69 tells the bee to follow its Lord’s made-easy paths, from which healing drink comes. This makes the source-section’s guided direction and useful finished vessel perceptible in a creature’s directed route and beneficial product.

luna: 16:71 names unequal provision among people and asks whether the favored will share it equally with those under their authority. This gives the source-section’s allotment of shares a concrete social consequence.

luna: 16:80 says God made animal hides into portable dwellings, light for travel and camping. The source-section’s measured, treated leather becomes a vessel; this verse gives the same material a concrete crafted use and purpose. | terra: God makes dwellings from cattle hides that are light in travel and settlement; this is the Quran’s clearest scene of hide deliberately turned into a useful constructed object.

luna: 16:96 says what people possess ends while what is with God remains. It sharpens the source-section’s worn waterskin and its statement that the Hereafter is more abiding. | terra: “What is with you runs out, and what is with God remains”; this gives the governing measure for the section’s worn object and its contrast between worldly and afterlife shares.
terra: Because they preferred worldly life over the Hereafter, God does not guide them; the wrong chosen share and the loss of direction are causally joined.
terra: The Abraham identified in 16:120 is chosen and guided to a straight path, directly connecting the surah’s named patriarch with fitted direction.

luna: 17:9 says the Qur’an guides to what is most upright. The source-section links ه د ي to an arrowhead aimed forward and س و ي to straightening what is crooked; this verse joins those two ideas in a guided, upright way.
terra: Whoever wants the immediate life receives only whatever God wills and apportions, then reaches Hell; even the chosen nearer share remains under the true measurer’s will.
terra: Whoever wants the Hereafter and strives for it faithfully has that striving thanked; this is the valid alternative to 17:18’s hastened but terminal worldly portion.
terra: Both groups are extended gifts “from your Lord,” and His giving is not barred; the ayah identifies the real giver behind all shares before 17:21 compares their ranks.
terra: Worldly gifts differ in rank, but the Hereafter has greater degrees and greater preference; it relocates the lottery arrow’s “highest” share into the enduring order.
terra: The Lord expands provision for whom He wills and measures it narrowly; worldly allotments are deliberate and informed, not winnings from a random shaft.

luna: 17:35 commands full measure and a straight balance. This is a direct practical counterpart to the source-section’s careful measurement before cutting, and makes fair measuring the boundary against manipulated shares.

luna: 17:83 says that when a person receives favor, he turns away and withdraws, using نَأَىٰ بِجَانِبِهِ. The source-section’s root ج ن ب names both the two sides of a vessel and avoiding the reminder; this verse joins the side-word to turning away from favor.
terra: The believer asks whether his companion rejects the one who created him from dust, then a drop, then proportioned him as a man; human form is a completed, staged product.
terra: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while lasting righteous deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; the apparent share is weighed against what remains.
terra: Iron blocks are heated until they become fire and then fused with molten copper; heat here likewise serves skilled straightening and assembly rather than only punishment.
terra: God says He made the revelation easy on the Prophet’s tongue so he could give good news and warn, closely matching ease granted to the messenger for the work of reminder.
terra: If the Prophet speaks aloud, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden; this closely repeats 87:7’s pairing of the overt (الجهر) with the hidden.
terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes either to bring a brand or “find guidance at the fire”; fire and هدى meet explicitly, illuminating the dictionary image of a fire-straightened guiding staff.

terra: Moses describes his staff as a tool for support and herding; its lived role as a carried guide gives a concrete object to the section’s dictionary claim that a staff is called hādī because it goes before its bearer.
terra: After Moses’ successive rescues and years in Midian, God says, “then you came according to a measure”; a guided life arrives at its prepared time and place.

luna: Moses answers Pharaoh that the Lord “أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ”: each thing receives its created form and then guidance. This states the source-section’s movement from making a thing fit to directing it. | terra: Moses defines “our Lord” as the one who gave every thing its created form and then guided it; this is the closest full parallel to the craftsman-like sequence “created/proportioned, measured/guided.”

luna: 20:74 says the criminal in Hell will neither die there nor live. This is a precise parallel to the source surah’s next statement after the great fire in 87:12, and clarifies the fire’s boundary condition.
terra: Passing worldly splendor is a test, whereas “your Lord’s provision is better and more lasting”; it matches the surah’s better, abiding alternative in the language of allotted sustenance.

luna: 21:47 sets up just scales for Resurrection and says no soul will be wronged even by a mustard seed. Against the source-section’s chance-drawn shares, it marks the boundary of exact, just accounting.
terra: Jonah thinks God will not “constrain” him; this probable restriction-sense of the قدر root offers a boundary case where measure is experienced as enclosure rather than fitting or allotment.

luna: 22:5 describes human formation from dust through successive womb stages, including formed and unformed, until birth and maturity. This is a specific bodily counterpart to the source-section’s stepwise craft and definition of ر ب ب as bringing a thing to completion. | terra: The long sequence from dust and drop through womb, birth, maturity, death, and decrepitude displays creation as preparation through successive states to differing limits.

luna: 22:36 describes sacrificial camels whose sides fall, then directs people to eat and feed others from them. The source-section’s meysir divides a slaughtered camel by lot; this verse gives a specific, pious distribution instead, and its “sides” also meet the source-section root ج ن ب.

luna: 22:37 says the meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does. It completes 22:36’s sharing of camel meat and contrasts a game’s material prize with the intention that makes an offering acceptable.
terra: Immediately after idols are said unable to create even a fly, people are said not to appraise God with His true appraisal; created power and failed human measuring confront each other.

luna: 23:12 begins the human’s making from an extract of clay. The source-section defines the root ر ب ب as bringing a thing state by state to completion; this is the first material stage in the adjacent account.
luna: 23:13 places the drop in a firm resting place, the next protected stage after 23:12 in the bodily sequence that illustrates the source-section’s definition of ر ب ب as gradual formation.

luna: 23:14 gives successive transformations of the drop and ends with another creation. This staged shaping gives a bodily counterpart to the source-section’s measured making and its definition of ر ب ب as bringing a thing to completion state by state. | terra: The embryo passes through several fashioned states and becomes another creation; “best of creators” marks the completed result of the staged craft.
terra: God sends water down from heaven “in measure” and settles it in the earth; measured liquid and a prepared repository echo the section’s making of a vessel to hold water.
luna: 23:102 says those whose scales are heavy are the successful. It joins measured weight to the success word that the source-section also connects to the share-arrow prohibition in 5:90.
luna: 23:103 says those whose scales are light have lost themselves and remain in Hell. It completes the opposite measured outcome and fire that frame the source-section’s choice of shares.

luna: 25:2 says God created everything and “فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقْدِيرًا.” The source-section’s craft reading of خَلَقَ as measuring before cutting makes the verse’s creation-with-measure sequence concrete. | terra: God created every thing and determined it with exact determination (فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقْدِيرًا), making measure intrinsic to creation rather than a later lottery of shares.

luna: Abraham says of God, “ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَنِى فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ.” The source-section cites this same pairing of creation and guidance, here spoken by Abraham as his account of dependence on his Lord. | terra: Abraham says that the one who created him is the one who guides him; his wording unites the two acts and also answers the surah’s final naming of Abraham’s scrolls.
terra: The she-camel has a drinking share and the people a drinking share on a known day; both portion and appointed time are fixed together.
luna: 26:181 commands full measure. In Shuayb’s speech this directly contrasts the source-section’s measured craft with the injustice of taking or giving portions by crooked means.
luna: 26:182 commands weighing with a straight balance. It specifies the just instrument in the same passage as 26:181, echoing the source-section’s straightening of a crooked thing.
luna: 26:183 forbids depriving people of their goods. It completes the measurement warning of 26:181–182 by naming the loss caused when shares are not fairly measured.
terra: The moving mountains are called “the workmanship of God, who perfected every thing”; explicit craft language supports the section’s hearing creation as skilled fabrication.
terra: Moses asks that his Lord guide him to the level or right way (سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ), joining guidance to the section’s straight/even vocabulary.

luna: 28:60 calls worldly gifts enjoyment and says what is with God is better and more lasting. This directly clarifies the source-section’s choice between the near life and the abiding one. | terra: Whatever people are given is worldly use and adornment, while what is with God is better and more lasting; a received share is judged by its endpoint.
terra: “Your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice” joins making to the assignment of an outcome and places selection with the Creator rather than with those drawing a lot.

luna: 28:77 says to seek the Hereafter through what God gave and not forget one’s share of the world. It gives a specific alternative to the source-section’s warning about preferring this life over the more lasting one. | terra: The addressee must seek the afterlife home with what God has given while not forgetting his worldly share (نَصِيبَكَ); a granted portion is material for the higher choice, not its rival.
terra: After envying Qarun, the observers recognize that God expands and restricts provision and that Qarun’s apparent winning share was no sign of final success.
terra: Every thing perishes except God’s face, while judgment belongs to Him and all return to Him; passing possession, final decision, and endpoint meet in one ayah.
terra: God expands provision for some servants and measures it narrowly for others; differing portions remain within His knowledge of every thing.
terra: Expansion and measured restriction of provision are called a sign, asking the recipients to read fluctuating shares as divine ordering.

luna: 30:54 describes the human moving from weakness to strength and back to weakness and old age. It makes the source-section’s definition of ر ب ب as bringing a thing through states concrete in the lifespan. | terra: God carries humans from weakness to strength and back to weakness and grey hair; the state-by-state arc concretizes nurture toward a determined bodily end.

luna: 32:7 says God made good everything He created. This fits the source-section’s shaped-arrow image as purposeful workmanship, though the verse describes creation broadly. | terra: God “made excellent the creation of every thing” and begins human creation from clay, stressing the fitted quality of the created product.
terra: After beginning the human from clay and offspring, God proportions him and gives him faculties; تسوية is one finishing stage in a larger manufacture.
terra: “God’s command is a measure measured” (قَدَرًا مَّقْدُورًا) presents an enacted matter as already delimited, reinforcing the dictionary sense of an assigned endpoint.
terra: David is commanded to make ample coats of mail and “measure precisely in the links” (وَقَدِّرْ فِى ٱلسَّرْدِ); it is a literal workshop scene of planning, fitting, and finishing parts.
terra: Those who reject the message cite their wealth and children, but God says the Lord expands or restricts provision; material size is not the measure of their final standing.
terra: The Lord expands or restricts provision and replaces whatever is spent; the true apportioner can renew a share rather than merely divide a fixed carcass.
terra: Creation from dust and then a drop, hidden pregnancy, and every lengthened or shortened life written in a book join bodily making to its measured span.

luna: 35:36 says the disbelievers in Hell are not put to death and their punishment is not lightened. This parallels the condition after the source-section’s great fire, though it states the death boundary rather than its full “nor live” wording.
terra: The sun runs toward its appointed resting point, “the measuring of the Mighty, the Knowing”; measure here includes both directed motion and a destination, like the fitted arrow’s point.
terra: God measures the moon through stations until it returns like an old date stalk; the verse makes measure a course with a visible end and also lets a made form age into thinness.
terra: People have benefits and drinks from the cattle God subjected to them; this cautiously links the animal source, benefit, and drink that converge materially in the section’s hide water vessel.
terra: God makes fire for people from the green tree and they kindle from it, presenting fire as a divinely prepared usable material.
terra: God guides Moses and Aaron to the straight path; the Moses named in 37:114 and in Surah 87’s closing scrolls is given the section’s directed course.

luna: 37:141 says Jonah “فَسَاهَمَ” and was among those who lost the lot. This is another concrete lot-drawing scene; its dangerous outcome differs from meysir’s distribution of a prize. | terra: Jonah participates in a drawing of lots and becomes one of the losers; it is a Quranic lot scene in which an assigned outcome directs a person’s next course.
terra: The repeated declaration that God will proportion the human before breathing spirit into him preserves the same craft sequence in a second passage.
terra: God creates people in their mothers’ wombs “creation after creation” through three darknesses, enacting the section’s definition of lordly nurture as stage-by-stage formation.
terra: Those who avoid false gods and turn back to God receive good news, showing avoidance as a saving orientation rather than the wretched person’s avoidance of reminder.
terra: The repeated question whether they know God expands and restricts provision makes recognition of the giver, rather than possession of the portion, the ayah’s sign.
terra: People do not appraise God with His true appraisal, while the whole earth and folded heavens display His scale; human estimation fails before the divine measurer’s cosmic grasp.
terra: The believer calls worldly life only temporary enjoyment and the Hereafter the lasting home, explicitly measuring the two offered destinations.
terra: God forms people and makes their forms good, provides good things, and is then identified as “your Lord”; fashioned form, provision, and lordship are one continuous care.

luna: 40:67 traces a person from dust and a drop through birth, maturity, old age, and an appointed term. It joins the source-section’s staged formation to its claim that a thing has a measure and endpoint. | terra: God brings people from dust and a drop through childhood to maturity and an appointed term, making both stepwise nurture and its endpoint explicit.
terra: God measures the earth’s provisions in four days, “equal for those who ask”; قَدَّرَ and سَوَآءً meet in an act that fits and apportions sustenance.
terra: God proportions the heaven as seven heavens, assigns each its command, and calls the result the determination of the Mighty, the Knowing; it completes the measured provisioning of 41:10.

luna: 41:51 repeats that upon favor a person “نَأَىٰ بِجَانِبِهِ” and turns aside. It makes the source-section’s ج ن ب branch for keeping away concrete as a response to provision, not just a vessel’s sides.
terra: Possessor of heaven’s and earth’s keys, God expands and restricts provision; ownership of the storehouses grounds His authority to allot.

luna: 42:20 contrasts the harvest of the Hereafter with the harvest of this world and says the latter-seeker has no afterlife share. It makes the source-section’s choice between near and lasting shares explicit. | terra: Whoever seeks the harvest of the Hereafter receives increase, while the seeker of the worldly harvest receives some of it but has no afterlife share; choice becomes an apportionment with a final consequence.

luna: 42:27 says God sends provision down by measure as He wills, since unrestricted abundance would lead people to transgress. It connects the source-section’s measured share to provision and marks a limit on abundance. | terra: God does not spread provision without limit because people would transgress; He sends it by whatever measure He wills, making limitation part of preparation and care.

luna: 42:36 likewise contrasts worldly enjoyment with what remains with God. Its description of the enduring portion makes the source-section’s better, lasting afterlife a concrete counterweight to a worldly share. | terra: Whatever people are given is merely worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more lasting for believers; the verse states the same boundary between temporary and enduring portions.
terra: Water descends from heaven by measure and revives a dead land; its allotted quantity is directed to a life-giving end rather than assigned by chance.

luna: 43:32 says God apportioned people’s livelihoods and raised some over others in rank. It is a direct counterpart to the source-section’s shares, while locating their distribution in God’s ordering rather than a lottery. | terra: God asks whether people distribute their Lord’s mercy, then says He distributes their livelihood in worldly life; divine apportionment displaces human claims to assign the decisive share.
terra: Gold and comparable splendor are only worldly enjoyment, while the Hereafter with the Lord belongs to the God-fearing; the “highest” material lot is displaced by the enduring award.
terra: God says He made the Quran easy in the Prophet’s tongue so that people might remember; the messenger’s ease is explicitly for remembrance.
terra: The condemned are told they used up their good things and enjoyed them in worldly life; their exhausted portion yields humiliation in the Hereafter.
terra: The Prophet is told to remind with the Quran whoever fears the warning, specifying fear as the condition that makes reminder reach its addressee.
terra: “Remind, for the reminder benefits the believers” directly resolves 87:9’s conditional wording and also returns the ordinary Quranic sense of نفع to the root used for a water-skin side piece.
terra: The question whether humans receive males while assigning females to God states the proposed division that 53:22 identifies as unjust.
terra: After 53:21 states the proposed gendered assignment, this ayah calls it an unjust division (قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ); not every humanly declared share is a straight measure.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn from one who turns from God’s reminder and desires only worldly life, directly joining failed reminder to the lower choice.
terra: This is called the limit of their knowledge, while the Lord best knows who strays and who is guided; it gives 53:29’s choice both a boundary and a directional judgment.
luna: 53:39 says a person has only what he strives for. This gives a specific alternative to the source-section’s lot-drawn meysir share: the afterlife portion follows effort rather than chance.
luna: 53:40 says the effort will be seen. It adds the accounting step between striving and repayment, clarifying how the source-section’s afterlife share is measured.
luna: 53:41 says the effort will then be repaid in full. It completes 53:39–40 with an allotted outcome based on deeds, against the source-section’s chance-assigned game share.
terra: God creates the male and female pair; 53:46 identifies the single emitted drop from which this differentiated making begins.
terra: The created pair of 53:45 comes from an emitted drop, supplying the small measured material from which distinct forms are assigned.
terra: God has made the Quran easy for remembrance and asks whether anyone will remember; ease and effective reminder are made one act.
terra: The repeated statement that the Quran is made easy for remembrance supplies another explicit occurrence of the same ease-to-reminder relation.
terra: The water is declared a division among the people and the she-camel, with each turn attended; measured access to water becomes an announced share rather than chance.
terra: This third refrain again joins divine easing of the Quran to the possibility of taking reminder, confirming that the formulation governs successive warning scenes.
terra: The fourth refrain preserves the same promise that a made-easy revelation can become remembrance for a receptive hearer.

luna: 54:49 says “إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَٰهُ بِقَدَرٍۢ”: everything created by measure, directly matching the source-section’s root ق د ر and its claim that every thing has an extent and term. | terra: “We created every thing by measure” (خَلَقْنَٰهُ بِقَدَرٍ) states directly the section’s claim that each made thing has an assigned measure.
terra: The sun and moon move by exact calculation, a compact repeated formulation of celestial bodies governed by measure.
luna: 55:7 says God set “ٱلْمِيزَانَ,” the balance. This makes ordered measure itself visible beside the source-section’s measured crafting and assigned shares.
luna: 55:8 commands not to transgress the balance, giving the source-section’s measure a moral boundary rather than leaving it as technique alone.
luna: 55:9 commands people to establish weight with justice and not diminish the balance. It completes the balance passage as a concrete ethical counterpart to measuring and dividing shares.
terra: Everyone upon the earth will pass away, supplying the finite endpoint against which any worldly allotment must be measured.
terra: The face of the Lord of majesty and honor remains after 55:26’s universal passing, identifying what outlasts every used-up share.
terra: “We have apportioned death among you” makes determination an inescapable distributed limit, directly illustrating the dictionary claim that every thing has a measure and a term.
terra: The question about the fire people kindle introduces fire as a humanly used tool whose source is then traced to divine making.
terra: God asks whether people created the fire’s tree or He did, relocating the useful flame inside the Creator’s craft.
terra: God makes the fire a reminder and a provision for travelers, joining its practical benefit to its work as remembrance.
terra: After the useful fire of 56:71–73, the command is to glorify the name of the Lord, the Great; crafted provision culminates in the same form of command as 87:1.
terra: “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Great” is a direct repeated command with the same speaker, object, and act as 87:1.

luna: 57:20 compares worldly life to vegetation that grows after rain then dries and becomes debris. It makes passing worldly provision visible beside the source-section’s worn vessel and the claim that the Hereafter remains.
terra: Every earthly or bodily event is in a book before God brings it into being; prior specification parallels the hide measured before it is cut and creation planned before its finished form.

luna: 59:7 assigns communal wealth to named recipients and says it should not circulate only among the rich. It gives a specific, ordered distribution in contrast to the source-section’s game-based shares.
terra: “The Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner” presents divine making through distinct craft-like names, followed by the glorification that 87:1 commands.
terra: God creates the heavens and earth with truth and forms people well, then says the destination is to Him; good formation is directed toward an end.

luna: 65:3 says God has set “قَدْرًا” for everything and mentions provision from where one does not expect. It directly combines the source-section’s root ق د ر with an allotted provision. | terra: “God has made for every thing a measure” (قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدْرًا) is the section’s “every thing has an amount and term” stated as a universal rule.
terra: Whoever fears God is given ease in his affair, joining the fearing recipient of reminder to divinely prepared ease.
terra: The seven layered heavens show no disparity in the Merciful’s creation; the invitation to inspect them for a fissure makes sound proportion visibly testable.
terra: The closing command to glorify the name of the Lord, the Great supplies another exact speaker-level parallel to the surah’s opening command.
terra: “You were created in stages” (خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا) condenses the section’s account of bringing a thing through successive states toward completion.
terra: God measures night and day, knows people cannot calculate them fully, and permits whatever recitation is easy (مَا تَيَسَّرَ); divine measuring and granted ease meet in one ayah.
terra: The denier “thought and calculated” (فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ), exactly the section’s planning sense of قدّر, but he applies skilled deliberation to fabricating a verdict against revelation.
terra: The curse “how he calculated” condemns the calculation begun in 74:18, marking a moral boundary between exact planning and its corrupt use.
terra: The repeated curse on how he calculated intensifies the boundary: the root’s craft-like intelligence does not validate the false product it prepares.
luna: 75:3 asks whether a person thinks God cannot assemble his bones. It sets up 75:4’s exact proportioning of fingertips, giving the source-section’s shaping image a resurrection counterpart.

luna: 75:4 says God can proportion even the fingertips. Its root س و ي directly meets the source-section’s straightening and shaping of an arrow, here applied to the exact reconstruction of a human body.
terra: “You love the immediate” states the choice of the nearer life in the same preference structure developed from Surah 87’s apportioned lot.
terra: “And leave the Hereafter” supplies the abandoned alternative that makes 75:20’s love a losing selection rather than mere enjoyment.
terra: From the clot God “created and proportioned” (فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ), repeating 87:2 within the staged making of a human.

luna: 76:3 says God guided the human to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful. The source-section’s arrow-point gloss for ه د ي becomes a path with two possible responses. | terra: God guides the human to the path, whether he becomes grateful or ungrateful; one directed way opens into opposed human responses.
terra: Paradisal silver vessels are “measured with exact measure” (قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا), a finished container whose capacity is fitted as precisely as the section’s cut hide vessel.
terra: People love the immediate life and leave behind a heavy day; the object of preference and its ignored endpoint mirror the section’s two possible shares.

luna: 77:20 asks whether God created people from a lowly fluid. This is another concrete creation passage corresponding to the source-section root خ ل ق and its image of shaping a thing from its starting material. | terra: The sequence begins by creating the human from lowly water; 77:21–23 then show the placement, known limit, and measuring that complete this cited row’s act of creation.

luna: 77:21 says the fluid was placed in a firm resting place. It adds the protected preparation stage after 77:20, paralleling the source-section’s making and fitting before completion. | terra: God places the drop in a secure resting place, giving the section’s abstract preparation a concrete fitted receptacle; 77:22 supplies its limit and 77:23 its measuring.

luna: 77:22 says the fluid remains there for a known term. It makes the source-section’s dictionary sense of ق د ر as extent and endpoint concrete in a measured period of human formation. | terra: The embryo remains “until a known measure” (إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ), displaying both the assigned amount and the terminal point named in the section’s dictionary sense.

luna: 77:23 says God determined the process and is an excellent determiner. It completes the creation, protected place, and appointed term of 77:20–22 with the source-section’s root ق د ر. | terra: After the drop is lodged until a known measure in 77:20–22, “We measured, and excellent are We at measuring” makes divine determination the governing act of the whole gestational scene.
terra: “Every thing We have enumerated in a record” gives a nonlexical parallel for creation in which nothing escapes prior count.
terra: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to his Lord so that he might fear, joining guidance, lordship, and the fear that makes reminder effective.
terra: Pharaoh claims “I am your lord, the highest,” a direct false reversal of the true “your Lord, the Most High” whom the surah commands the Prophet to glorify.
terra: God raised the heaven’s structure and proportioned it (فَسَوَّىٰهَا), presenting تسوية as the finishing of a vast constructed form.
terra: The transgressor “preferred the worldly life,” an almost verbal restaging of the choice in 87:16.
terra: Hell becomes the refuge of the chooser in 79:38, showing where the apparently preferable near-world share is directed.
terra: The alternative person fears standing before his Lord and restrains desire, supplying the opposite criterion for choosing a share.
terra: Paradise is the refuge of the person in 79:40, completing the two apportioned destinations.

luna: 80:19 says “خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ” of the human being: creation followed by measured determination, the same sequence as the source-section roots خ ل ق and ق د ر. | terra: From a sperm-drop God “created him, then measured him” (خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ), reproducing the section’s creation-as-prior-measure in one human-making act.

luna: 80:20 continues “ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ”: after creation and measure, the way is made easy. This directly joins the source-section roots ق د ر and ي س ر as measure followed by facilitated direction. | terra: After 80:19’s creation and measuring, God makes the path easy (ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ); the sequence joins measured making, direction, and ease exactly as this section joins 87:2, 87:3, and 87:8.

luna: 82:7 says God “خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ,” creating, proportioning, and balancing the human. Its sequence closely echoes the source-section’s خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ and the straightening of a shaped object. | terra: The human is addressed by the Lord “who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you”; the sequence turns creation into the fitting and straightening of a made body.
luna: 82:8 says God composed the human in whatever form He willed. Following 82:7, it adds the chosen form to the source-section’s image of measuring, shaping, and preparing an object.
luna: 83:1 condemns those who give short measure. It supplies a specific ethical reversal of the source-section’s careful measurement before cutting and its allotted shares.
luna: 83:2 describes sellers who take full measure from others. It specifies one side of the double standard in 83:1–3, clarifying the abuse against which proper measure stands.
luna: 83:3 says they give less when measuring or weighing for others. It completes the reversal of careful measure: the tool of allotment is manipulated to deprive another.
luna: 83:4 asks whether those who short measure expect to be raised. It continues 83:1–3 from fraudulent measurement to the afterlife reckoning that the source-section connects with measured shares.
luna: 83:5 identifies the resurrection as a great day. It specifies the horizon of judgment introduced in 83:4, linking unjust measure to the source-section’s lasting afterlife portion.
luna: 83:6 says people will stand before the Lord of the worlds. It completes 83:4–5’s reckoning and gives a concrete account of the source-section’s share assigned by the Lord.
luna: 89:15 describes a person mistaking generous provision for honor. The next verse uses قَدَرَ for restricted provision, making this a concrete question of how an allotted share should be read.

luna: 89:16 says God “قَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ,” restricting provision, while the person mistakes this for humiliation. It completes 89:15 and clarifies that measured shares are not a simple worldly ranking. | terra: When the Lord measures a person’s provision narrowly, he says his Lord has humiliated him; the ayah exposes the human error of treating the size of a share as its worth.

luna: 91:7 swears by the soul and the One who “سَوَّىٰهَا.” This is the source-section’s root س و ي in the concrete scene of a proportioned creature. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who proportioned it presents the inner person as a deliberately fitted creation.

luna: 91:8 says the soul was inspired with its wickedness and piety; after 91:7’s proportioning, it gives a moral direction to the formed soul, completing the source-section’s claim that what is made is also turned toward a way. | terra: After the soul is proportioned in 91:7, it is inspired with both its wickedness and its piety; fitted creation is followed by disclosure of the two possible directions.
luna: 91:9 says “قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا.” Its success and purification join the source-section’s mention of the successful person in 87:14 to the outcome of a rightly directed life.

luna: 91:10 says the one who buries the soul fails, the reversal of 91:9’s purified soul and of the source section’s successful outcome; it makes the measure-and-guidance image a fork with contrary results.
luna: 92:5 begins the giving-and-fearing route that leads to ease in 92:7. It parallels the source-section’s successful, purified choice and helps specify who is being eased.
luna: 92:6 says the giver affirms the best, completing the disposition before 92:7’s ease. It clarifies that the source-section’s direction is tied to response, not chance.

luna: 92:7 says “فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ,” easing a person toward ease. This repeats the source-section root ي س ر and specifies one direction of the life-choice its prose links to 87:8 and 87:16–17. | terra: “We shall ease him toward ease” repeats 87:8’s formula; 92:5–6 make giving, fear, and affirmation the acts that orient this directed easing.
luna: 92:8 introduces the miser who feels self-sufficient, the opposite disposition to 92:5 and a concrete version of the source-section’s preference for worldly life.
luna: 92:9 says this person denies the best, explaining the turning away that leads to hardship in 92:10 and echoes 87:11.

luna: 92:10 says a person may be eased toward hardship, using the source-section root ي س ر in a reversed outcome. It gives a specific opposite to 87:8’s ease and aligns with the source-section’s wretched person who avoids the reminder and enters fire. | terra: “We shall ease him toward hardship” reverses the same formula: facilitation can direct a person toward a ruinous endpoint when his prior choice is denial and withholding.
luna: 92:11 says wealth will not avail when its owner falls. It qualifies the source-section’s worldly shares with the limit that a game’s or life’s wealth cannot secure the final outcome.
luna: 92:12 says “إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ,” placing guidance upon God. This directly parallels the source-section’s ه د ي and its claim that making includes directing.

luna: 92:13 says the first life and the Hereafter belong to God. It grounds the source-section’s contrast between choosing the lowly near life and the more lasting afterlife in divine ownership of both.
luna: 92:14 warns of a blazing fire. It carries forward the source-section’s reference to entering the great fire in 87:12, with the next verses identifying who reaches it.

luna: 92:15 says only the most wretched will enter that fire. This gives a concrete counterpart to 87:11–12’s wretched person avoiding the reminder and entering fire. | terra: Only “the most wretched” will enter the blazing fire, closely matching 87:11–12’s wretched person who enters the greater fire and anchoring the fire-straightening word in its Quranic moral sense.
luna: 92:16 characterizes that wretched person as one who denies and turns away. It specifies the refusal behind the avoidance named in 87:11, rather than leaving the fire as an unchosen fate.

luna: 92:17 says the most God-fearing will be kept away from the fire, the reverse outcome to 92:15 and to the source-section’s wretched person entering it. | terra: “The most God-fearing will be kept away from it” reverses 92:15 and 87:11–12 through the same avoidance family: distance from the fire becomes salvation rather than refusal of reminder.

luna: 92:18 describes the God-fearing person as giving wealth to purify himself. It gives a concrete counterpart to the source-section’s successful person who purifies himself in 87:14. | terra: The person kept from fire gives wealth to purify himself, replacing the lottery’s attempt to acquire a portion with voluntary relinquishing of one.

luna: 92:20 says the giver seeks “وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ.” The source-section links the highest meysir arrow, المُعَلَّى, to ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ in 87:1; this verse redirects the highest aim from a game’s share to the Lord. | terra: He seeks only the face of “his Lord, the Most High” (رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَى), relocating the lot-arrow name for the highest share into the true highest object of choice.

luna: 92:21 promises that this person will be satisfied. It supplies the outcome of 92:18–20’s giving and seeking the Most High, a durable fulfillment alongside the source-section’s better, abiding Hereafter. | terra: “He will surely be satisfied” gives the giver in 92:18–20 his final granted outcome, completing the passage’s alternative economy of portion and reward.
terra: Humanity is created “in the finest proportion” (فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ), a bodily counterpart to the section’s smooth, straight, correctly fitted product.
luna: 99:7 says whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. The tiny but exact weight makes the source-section’s measured allotment concrete in judgment.
luna: 99:8 applies the same atom-weight test to evil. It completes the balanced accounting of 99:7 and shows the boundary between the two outcomes.
luna: 101:6 asks whose scales are heavy. The source-section’s measured portion and the lot’s high share are recast as a measured deed-weight that determines the afterlife outcome.
luna: 101:7 says the heavy-scaled person will be in a pleasant life, completing the measured outcome begun in 101:6 and contrasting with the source section’s fire.
luna: 101:8 asks whose scales are light, the opposite measurement to 101:6 and a counterpart to the source-section’s wretched outcome.
luna: 101:9 identifies the light-scaled person’s destination as the abyss. It completes the scale’s contrary outcome in 101:8, as the source section pairs success with fire for the wretched.
